record.original_question: In Theorem 8, one assumes a function psi(t) that increases to infinity and then constructs real numbers theta_1, theta_2, eta_1, eta_2 with inf_{x in Z_+} x psi(x) ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| > 0. Can the same conclusion still hold when psi(t) is the positive constant psi_0 for all t, rather than a function tending to infinity? If not, the paper notes that this would imply a stronger inhomogeneous version of Littlewood's conjecture.

evidence.quote: Theorem 8. Let ψ(t) be a function increasing to infinity as t → +∞. ... Then there exist real numbers θ1 , θ2 linearly independent over Z together with 1 and real numbers η1 , η2 such that inf xψ(x) · ||α1 x − η1 || · ||α2x − η2 || > 0.

The following problem is an open one: is it possible that for a constant function ψ(t) = ψ0 > 0 ∀t the conclusion of Theorem 8 remains true. If not, it means that a stronger inhomogeneous version of Littlewood conjecture is valid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Let $\mathbb{Z}_{+}$ denote the set of positive integers.

It is known that for every function $\psi:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ that increases to infinity as $t\to+\infty$, there exist real numbers $\theta_1,\theta_2$ that are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ together with $1$, and real numbers $\eta_1,\eta_2$, such that
$$\inf_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}} x\,\psi(x)\,\|x\theta_1-\eta_1\|\,\|x\theta_2-\eta_2\| \;>\; 0.$$

Question: Does the analogous statement remain true when $\psi$ is replaced by a positive constant? That is, does there exist a constant $\psi_0>0$ together with real numbers $\theta_1,\theta_2$ linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ with $1$, and real numbers $\eta_1,\eta_2$, such that
$$\inf_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}} x\,\|x\theta_1-\eta_1\|\,\|x\theta_2-\eta_2\| \;>\; 0\,?$$

Determine whether such $\theta_1,\theta_2,\eta_1,\eta_2$ exist. (A negative answer would imply a strong inhomogeneous form of Littlewood's conjecture, namely that for all real $\theta_1,\theta_2,\eta_1,\eta_2$ with $\theta_1,\theta_2,1$ linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, $\inf_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}} x\,\|x\theta_1-\eta_1\|\,\|x\theta_2-\eta_2\|=0$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly stated as open. Littlewood's conjecture itself remains unsolved; the Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss result only shows the exceptional set has Hausdorff dimension zero. No source found establishing the constant-ψ inhomogeneous version, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Littlewood conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss have shown that the exceptional set ... must have Hausdorff dimension zero
status_evidence.claim: The classical Littlewood conjecture is still open; only partial measure-theoretic results are known.

status_evidence.title: On certain Littlewood-like and Schmidt-like problems in inhomogeneous Diophantine approximations
status_evidence.snippet: Moshchevitin: inhomogeneous approximations to two real numbers and badly approximable numbers
status_evidence.claim: Related inhomogeneous Littlewood-type problems are studied as open problems.
